## Introduction

In this activity, you complete and run a *targets* pipeline
that reads the selected `HealthWellbeing` version, pools the study
correlations, and writes a summary for the report. 

**The pipeline is
partially completed: you fill in two short gaps rather than writing it
from scratch. By the end, you should be able to trace the summary back
to its input and explain which steps targets reruns, and why.**

Work in your MyBinder session, after preparing
the dataset versions. If you fall behind, the **Get back on track** step
below restores a working pipeline so you can continue.
[Prepare the dataset versions](00_preparation.qmd#preparation-data)

## The pipeline at a glance

A *target* is one named step whose result *targets* stores and
tracks. When a target's code mentions another target by name, it
depends on that target. The analysis has four stages:

``` text
select input -> check studies -> fit meta-analysis -> write summary
```

| Stage | Numbered steps in the script | Targets | Your gap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Select input | 1–3 | `version_file`, `data_version`, `dataset_file` | None |
| Check studies | 4 | `studies` | None |
| Fit meta-analysis | 5 | `fit` | TODO 1 connects `studies` to `fit` |
| Write summary | 6–7 | `result`, `summary_file` | TODO 2 writes the summary file |

The checked studies also feed a second output: the linear regression predictive model
from the versioning demonstration. The summary records that model's
version.

``` text
check studies -> train and pin predictive model -> model version in the summary
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Every target and its dependencies

``` text
version_file -> data_version -> dataset_file -> studies -> fit
dataset_file, data_version -> data_provenance
studies, data_provenance, data_version -> predictive_model -> model_pin_files -> model_version
fit, data_provenance, data_version, model_version, pipeline_file -> result -> summary_file
```

`version_file`, `dataset_file`, and `summary_file` are file targets:
*targets* tracks the contents of the selection file, the pinned RDS
file, and the summary CSV. `pipeline_file` tracks the analysis script and
its checksum.
:::

The model uses the raw Pearson correlations and study sample sizes.
*meta* transforms each correlation to Fisher's z scale and pools the
effects with a random-effects model. We use restricted maximum
likelihood (REML) to estimate between-study variance and the
Hartung–Knapp method for the 95% confidence interval of the pooled
correlation. The summary converts the estimate and limits back to the
correlation scale. It also records between-study heterogeneity and a
95% prediction interval, which the report lesson explains.

This model treats study summaries as independent and assumes their
correlations address a comparable association. Differences in
populations, measures, and sampling limit interpretation. This is a
worked example of pooling reported effects from the supplied studies
[@harrer2021, sec. 4.2.4].

## Step 1: copy the workbook pipeline

Run this code. It loads the
*targets* functions and copies the partially completed template to
`workspace/_targets.R`, your own working copy. The copy is only made
if it does not exist yet, so rerunning the chunk keeps your edits.
Git ignores the `workspace/` folder, so the supplied template stays
unchanged.

```{r health-targets-setup, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
source("pipelines/workshop_support.R")
use_workshop_book_outputs()

box::use(
  targets[tar_make, tar_network, tar_outdated, tar_read, tar_visnetwork]
)
invisible(loadNamespace("visNetwork")) # Load the graph display package quietly.

source("pipelines/workshop_support.R")
workshop_dir <- workshop_output_dir()
pipeline_template <- file.path(
  "pipelines", "exercise", "_targets_health_wellbeing.R"
)
pipeline_script <- file.path("workspace", "_targets.R")
pipeline_store <- file.path(workshop_dir, "_targets")

dir.create("workspace", showWarnings = FALSE)
if (!file.exists(pipeline_script)) {
  file.copy(pipeline_template, pipeline_script)
}

```

## Step 2: run the pipeline before completing it

Open `workspace/_targets.R` in RStudio and
read the numbered steps. Then draw the dependency graph and
try to run the pipeline.

```{r health-targets-first-run, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
tar_visnetwork(
  script = pipeline_script,
  store = pipeline_store,
  targets_only = TRUE,
  outdated = TRUE
)
tar_make(script = pipeline_script, store = pipeline_store)
```

Nothing connects `result` to `summary_file` and the `fit` step has thrown an error. The run stops at a TODO placeholder.

## Solution to TODO 1

``` r
      data = studies,
```

Mentioning `studies` makes `fit` depend on it, so the graph gains an
arrow from `studies` to `fit`.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution to TODO 2

``` r
      utils::write.csv(result, path, row.names = FALSE)
      path
```

A file target returns the path of the file it wrote. *targets* then
tracks the file's contents and rebuilds it if the file changes.
:::

## Step 4: inspect the graph and run the pipeline {#check-dependencies}

Run the pipeline again and read the result.

```{r health-targets-run, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
tar_make(script = pipeline_script, store = pipeline_store)
tar_read(result, store = pipeline_store)
```

Check that your own pipeline is complete by drawing the graph again.

```{r health-targets-graph, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
tar_visnetwork(
  script = pipeline_script,
  store = pipeline_store,
  targets_only = TRUE,
  outdated = FALSE
)
```

On the first complete run, targets with new or changed inputs report that they completed.
*targets* saves every result in the pipeline store, here
`outputs/health-wellbeing/_targets`, and `tar_read()` loads a saved
result without rerunning anything.

## Step 5: run it again

Run the pipeline a second time and ask which
targets are outdated.

```{r health-targets-rerun, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
tar_make(script = pipeline_script, store = pipeline_store)
tar_visnetwork(
  script = pipeline_script,
  store = pipeline_store,
  targets_only = TRUE,
  outdated = FALSE
)
```

Nothing runs, and no target is outdated. *targets* reruns a step only
when its code, its upstream targets, or its tracked files change.

## Checkpoint {#targets-checkpoint}

Refer to the bottom two steps of `workspace/_targets.R`. We have fitted a mixed-effect meta-analysis model and written the results to a CSV file: `outputs/health-wellbeing/meta-summary.csv`.

```{r meta-summary-view, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
read.csv(file.path(
  "outputs", "health-wellbeing", "meta-summary.csv"
)) |> 
  dplyr::select(c("data_version", "data_scope", "data_filter", "pooled_r", "confidence_level", "tau2", "effect_scale", "tau_method", "meta_version")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) |> 
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
      cols = everything(),
      names_to = "metric",
      values_to = "value",
      values_transform = list(value = as.character)
    ) 
```
